values.note: $13 a night for a single site, self-pay (or Scan and Pay in the recreation.gov app). Fees apply during the full-service summer period; when no services are provided in early spring and late fall, 'the fees at some areas are not charged'.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/moosehead-lake-campground ('Overnight Use: Single Site: $13 per night'; '24 hours - self pay'; 'Fees shown are for the summer recreation period when full services are provided. During the early spring and late fall when no services are provided the fees at some areas are not charged.'; page last updated May 5, 2026) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10192097 (Scan and Pay), read 2026-10-25

discounts.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/moosehead-lake-campground ('Golden Age/Interagency Access and Senior Passes accepted'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: First-come only: claim a site in person and self-pay, or pay by scanning the QR code with the recreation.gov app (Scan and Pay). Campers must occupy the site the first night.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/moosehead-lake-campground ('No reservations - first come, first serve.'; 'Camping in a developed recreation site is allowed for a period not longer than 14 days'; 'Campers must occupy the site the first night') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10192097 ('This location is available on a first-come, first-served basis only. Visitors are required to physically arrive at the campground to purchase and claim a site ... Scan and Pay'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Opens with full services the Friday before Memorial Day. From September 30 there is no water or garbage service, but the campground stays usable until snow reduces access or January 1, whichever is sooner.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/moosehead-lake-campground ('Seasons of Use May 22 – September 30'; 'Reduced services beginning September 30, 2026, no water or garbage services will be provided. Visitors can use the facility until snow conditions reduce access or January 1st, whichever is sooner.'; 'scheduled to open with full services the Friday before Memorial Day'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: One loop of 8 drive-in sites 'that can accommodate tents, trailers, and motorhomes' (no maximum length posted), screened by natural vegetation; one RV or camper trailer, two vehicles and eight people per site.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/moosehead-lake-campground ('No. of Sites: 8'; 'This campground provides drive-in sites that can accommodate tents, trailers, and motorhomes'; 'Eight people and 2 motorized vehicles are allowed per campsite with a maximum of one RV or camper trailer'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Two vault toilets in the loop and a centrally located pressurized faucet (no water after the September 30 service cutoff).

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/moosehead-lake-campground ('Two vault toilets are located in the camping loop, drinking water is provided at a centrally located pressurized faucet'; 'Potable water is available at this site.'), read 2026-10-25

note: Ottawa NF campground beside Moosehead Lake on the Wisconsin border, 10 mi SE of Marenisco (Bessemer RD); reached from M-64 by FR 8220, FR 6860 and FR 6862. A free concrete boat ramp next to the campground; a channel lets boats pass to Little Presque Isle Lake in Wisconsin. Northern pike, bass, muskellunge, crappie and bluegill. --Claude
summary: FS page (updated 2026-05-05) + recreation.gov: $13 single (confirmed), Senior/Access accepted (new), first-come only with self-pay or Scan and Pay (confirmed), 14-day limit (new), season May 22 - Sept 30 with reduced services to snow/Jan 1 (new), 8 drive-in sites for tents, trailers and motorhomes (new), vault toilets (confirmed) + pressurized faucet (new). recreation.gov catalog lists only management/scan-and-pay records, no reservable site. Run by the Forest Service (no concessionaire named). No Ottawa alert touches M-64 or FR 8220/6860/6862 (the Oct 9-10 rally closures were near Kenton). Note trimmed of field restatements.
